Context.title: High-value science is developed continuously. Much of it never reaches the market.
Context.body:
Universities and research centers generate discoveries with high therapeutic potential every year. The challenge rarely lies in the science itself, but in the ability to turn knowledge into protected, validated pharmaceutical assets ready for global production.

Without adequate technological maturation, scientific governance, and an intellectual property strategy, promising technologies remain confined to academia and never reach their full impact potential.

items.title: Asset De-risking and Development
items.text: We progressively reduce scientific, technological, and scale-up uncertainties through a structured development strategy. The goal is to advance promising technologies in maturity and build more robust pharmaceutical assets that are attractive to strategic partners and licensors.

items.title: Scientific and Regulatory Governance
items.text: We integrate scientific governance, technological development, and regulatory strategy from the earliest stages. Each asset evolves with decision criteria, development milestones, and evidence geared toward pharmaceutical development requirements and future licensing routes.

items.title: Intellectual Property Strategy and Consolidation
items.text: We structure intellectual property as a central element of the asset's value. We assess ownership, freedom to operate, and protection strategy to build IP portfolios that are consistent, defensible, and aligned with the asset's development and global licensing potential.

items.title: Global Positioning and Licensing
items.text: We prepare and position assets for connection with the global pharmaceutical ecosystem. We structure partnership, co-development, and licensing opportunities, bringing scientific assets closer to industries and strategic partners capable of taking them to their next stages of development.

Context.creationStatement: Between scientific discovery and the pharmaceutical industry, we build assets.

about.title: An integrated platform. Two complementary pillars.
about.body:
Aether Global Pharma and ICT AetherBio+ operate synergistically to transform high-potential science into structured pharmaceutical assets that advance along the development journey and generate value.

ICT AetherBio+ brings together scientific expertise, infrastructure, partners, and resources to advance projects and reduce their technological risk. Aether Global Pharma leads the assets' development and value-creation strategy, integrating intellectual property, regulatory strategy, capital, and positioning for partnerships and licensing.

Together, they connect universities and researchers, specialized capital, and the pharmaceutical industry, creating a structured journey for promising discoveries to advance with greater maturity, consistency, and global potential - expanding, for industry, access to selected, protected assets progressively developed for external innovation.

gp.body:
Aether Global Pharma is the platform's business pillar and operates as a Pharmaceutical Asset Venture Builder, dedicated to building, developing, and adding value to pharmaceutical assets originating from high-potential science.

The company leads the assets' integrated strategy, bringing together intellectual property, development, capital, and market positioning. It builds partnership, co-development, and licensing opportunities, connecting progressively developed assets to the pharmaceutical industry and specialized capital.
functions: Strategy, management, and value creation for the pharmaceutical asset portfolio
Ownership and strategic management of intellectual property assets
Engaging private capital and specialized life sciences investors
Developing partnerships with the pharmaceutical industry
Structuring co-development, licensing, royalty, milestone, and liquidity-event models

bio.body:
ICT AetherBio+ is the platform's scientific and technological pillar, responsible for bringing together expertise, infrastructure, and resources to advance and de-risk high-potential pharmaceutical projects.

As a nonprofit science, technology, and innovation institution, it oversees the projects' scientific governance and builds development strategies aimed at advancing technology readiness. It connects researchers, universities, research centers, and specialized partners, mobilizing scientific and technological capabilities to generate evidence, reduce uncertainty, and prepare projects for their next development stages.

Its work also provides access to national and international funding and scientific cooperation mechanisms, backed by specialized, multidisciplinary governance.
functions: Scientific and technological de-risking aimed at building pharmaceutical assets
Scientific governance and structured management of technology-readiness advancement
Engagement with universities, research centers, CROs, and specialized partners
Structuring and qualifying scientific projects with translational potential
Securing and coordinating public funding and non-dilutive resources, both national and international
Generating evidence and advancing TRLs to reduce uncertainty and add value to assets

PDPage.metaDescription: Aether's scientific approach: TRL maturation, independent governance, and comprehensive intellectual property protection in pharmaceutical projects.
PDPage.heading: From scientific discovery to global pharmaceutical asset.
PDPage.heroText:
At Aether, research and development are oriented toward building value.

As a Pharmaceutical Asset Venture Builder, we identify and develop scientific discoveries with the potential to become protected, technically validated pharmaceutical assets, strategically positioned for licensing, industrial partnership, or other monetization transactions.

Each asset advances through a structured journey of scientific and technological de-risking, TRL maturation, intellectual property strategy, and specialized governance.
PDPage.contextTitle: A scientific discovery is not yet a pharmaceutical asset.
PDPage.approachText:
Turning science into a pharmaceutical asset takes more than generating experimental results. It requires identifying application potential, building intellectual protection, reducing critical uncertainties, and generating the evidence needed to progressively increase the asset's maturity and value.

At the Aether platform, development follows an asset-building logic: every scientific, technological, and strategic decision should help make the asset more robust, protectable, and attractive to future industrial partners, licensees, and specialized life sciences investors.

Scientific and technological execution is carried out in coordination with ICT AetherBio+, universities, research centers, specialists, and technology partners, within a governance structure defined for each asset.

items.title: Scientific and Technological De-risking
items.text: We identify each asset's critical uncertainties and structure its development to progressively reduce them. Scientific evidence generation, technological validation, and maturity advancement are guided by decision milestones, allowing capital and resources to be concentrated on assets that show greater consistency and value potential. The goal isn't just to advance the research - it's to increase the asset's quality and reliability.
items.alt: Scientific team analyzing imaging scans on a lab screen

items.title: Intellectual Property and Defensibility
items.text: Intellectual property is a central part of building the pharmaceutical asset. We assess ownership, novelty, protection potential, freedom to operate, and the strategy for expanding protection throughout development. Protected science stops being merely knowledge and becomes an intangible asset with the potential to generate economic value.
items.alt: Researcher using a microscope in an analysis laboratory

items.title: Specialized Scientific Governance
items.text: Each asset is accompanied by specialists selected according to its scientific, technological, and therapeutic nature. Scientific governance strengthens the quality of decisions, methodological rigor, and independent review of development milestones, supporting decisions to continue, redirect, or say NO GO. At Aether, moving forward also means knowing when not to.
items.alt: Team of scientists gathered in a laboratory for a scientific governance decision

items.title: Asset Maturation and Value Creation
items.text: Development is structured to progressively increase each asset's scientific, technological, and strategic maturity. As relevant risks are reduced, evidence is consolidated, and intellectual property is strengthened, the asset broadens its appeal to the pharmaceutical industry and specialized partners. Each advance should increase not just the TRL, but also the asset's strategic quality and monetization potential.
items.alt: Ascending podiums with a sprout, representing the asset's progressive maturation

PDPage.profileIntro: Aether identifies and selects scientific discoveries and health technologies with the potential to become protected, developable, and licensable pharmaceutical assets. We prioritize opportunities that show a consistent combination of the following attributes:

criterios.title: Robust scientific grounding
criterios.text: Hypotheses backed by experimental evidence, technically consistent methodology, and data that allow critical analysis, validation, and the definition of the next development milestones.

criterios.title: Translational potential
criterios.text: A concrete possibility of transforming the scientific discovery into a therapeutic solution or technology applicable to pharmaceutical development.

criterios.title: Intellectual property potential
criterios.text: The ability to build or strengthen an intellectual property position that contributes to the asset's exclusivity, defensibility, and strategic value.

criterios.title: Development and monetization potential
criterios.text: A technically viable development pathway and a clear hypothesis for generating value through licensing, strategic partnership, technology transfer, or another transaction related to the asset.

PDPage.profileFooter: Opportunities can originate at universities, STIs, research centers, scientific startups, independent researchers, and other innovation organizations, in Brazil or abroad.

responsaveis.bio:
Coordinator of the Center for Medicinal Chemistry (CQMED-Unicamp), an Embrapii Industrial Innovation Unit in the Pharmaceuticals/Biopharmaceuticals field, since 2017. Researcher in RNA-binding proteins in disease, medicinal chemistry, bioinformatics, and recombinant proteins for diagnostics. Has more than 15 years of experience planning and executing research and innovation projects, with 46 high-impact international publications.

Coordinates international projects in RNA splicing and medicinal chemistry with the University of Oxford, University of California San Diego, Tübingen University, and the Structural Genomics Consortium (SGC) in Canada. In 2025 she received Embrapii's outstanding researcher award, and in 2024 was honored as an outstanding health research professional by the Campinas, SP City Council. She also serves as deputy coordinator of CBMEG and Coordinator of CIBIO-CBMEG.

Professor at Unicamp in Organic Synthesis, with an emphasis on asymmetric synthesis, drug and natural product synthesis, and biological activity evaluation. Coordinates the Chemistry area at CQMED-Unicamp. Holds patent applications related to preparation methods for pharmaceutical ingredients, including methylphenidate, tamoxifen, levobupivacaine, and fluoxetine.

Held senior academic and scientific management positions, including Director of the Institute of Chemistry and Provost for Research at Unicamp, as well as roles in strategic scientific policy bodies at CNPq and FAPESP, including vice-presidency of FAPESP's Superior Council.

Co-author of the textbook Substâncias Carboniladas e Derivados (Carbonyl Substances and Derivatives), a reference in Organic Chemistry with national and international English-language editions.

Received major national and international awards and honors, including the Zeferino Vaz Award (Unicamp), the Simão Mathias Medal (SBQ), the Israel Vargas Medal, and the BMOS Award. Member of the São Paulo State Academy of Sciences and the Brazilian Academy of Sciences.

TRLPage.metaTitle: TRL - Technology Readiness Level | Aether Global Pharma
TRLPage.metaDescription: The TRL 1-9 scale applied to pharmaceutical development, from scientific principle to commercialization. Based on ISO 16290 and the RBIF TRL Guide.
TRLPage.heading: Nine levels between scientific discovery and the global market.
TRLPage.heroText:
The Technology Readiness Level (TRL) scale organizes a technology's maturity into nine levels, from observing fundamental principles to demonstration in an operational environment.

At Aether, this reference is applied to pharmaceutical development through an integrated approach, considering scientific evidence, technological maturity, nonclinical development, CMC, regulatory strategy, and preparation for transfer and licensing.
TRLPage.contextTitle: A common language for talking about risk, maturity, and value.
TRLPage.scaleText:
The TRL scale was originally developed by NASA and is now widely used as a reference for assessing the maturity of technologies in development.

In the pharmaceutical sector, its application requires contextual interpretation. An asset's progress doesn't happen in a purely linear way: scientific development, CMC, nonclinical studies, regulatory strategy, and clinical development advance in an integrated manner and can show different levels of maturity along the way.

At Aether, TRL is used as one of the axes for organizing asset progress, guiding development decisions, identifying gaps, planning evidence generation, structuring fundraising, and supporting intellectual property, technology transfer, and licensing strategies.

Each advance in maturity represents the generation of more robust evidence and the progressive reduction of scientific and technological uncertainty.
TRLPage.methodologyText: Aether uses the TRL scale as a reference for contextualized assessment of technological maturity, taking into account ISO 16290 and its application to pharmaceutical development.
TRLPage.journeyHeading: From the bench to the market, in three development phases.

jornada.subtitle: Scientific foundations
jornada.desc: Investigation of fundamental principles, hypothesis formulation, and generation of the first experimental evidence. The technology evolves from initial scientific knowledge to a proof of concept, with progressive assessment of its application potential.
jornada.onde: Universities, research centers, and academic laboratories.

jornada.subtitle: Validation and uncertainty reduction
jornada.desc: The technology advances from proof of concept to increasing levels of validation, integration, and demonstration under relevant conditions. Scientific, technological, and preclinical evidence is generated, accompanied by the progressive development of CMC, regulatory strategy, and technical documentation.
jornada.onde: Specialized laboratories, research centers, CROs, CDMOs, and technology and industrial partners.

jornada.subtitle: Proof and application
jornada.desc: The technology reaches advanced maturity levels, generating evidence in clinical and operational settings, regulatory qualification, preparation for scale production, and, when applicable, market approval and use.
jornada.onde: Clinical centers, CROs, the pharmaceutical industry, production units, and regulatory agencies.

TRLPage.levelsHeading: The complete scale, level by level.
TRLPage.levelsText: Click each level to see its description and a reference for its application in pharmaceutical development. The correspondence between TRL and pharmaceutical stages is contextual and may vary depending on each technology's nature and development strategy.

levels.name: Basic principles observed
levels.desc: Exploratory scientific research, identifying and observing the fundamental principles related to the technology. Knowledge is still at an early stage of investigation.
levels.pharma: Identification of targets, biological mechanisms, molecular classes, or candidate active ingredients; literature review and formulation of the first scientific hypotheses.

levels.name: Technology concept formulated
levels.desc: Fundamental principles begin to be translated into a potential application. Scientific and technological hypotheses are formulated and the first paths for their validation are defined.
levels.pharma: Definition of the therapeutic concept, initial candidate selection, proposed mechanism of action, and planning of the first feasibility studies.

levels.name: Experimental proof of concept
levels.desc: Initial experimental evidence demonstrates the concept's feasibility. The hypothesis is tested under controlled conditions, and the first results allow the technology's potential to be assessed.
levels.pharma: In vitro assays, analytical studies, initial characterization, and generation of preliminary evidence of the asset's activity, mechanism, or feasibility.

levels.name: Validation in a laboratory environment
levels.desc: The technology's main components are integrated and validated in a controlled environment. The proof of concept evolves into a more robust and reproducible configuration.
levels.pharma: Expanded asset characterization, initial optimization, analytical development, formulation or process studies, and generation of efficacy evidence in appropriate experimental models.

levels.name: Validation in a relevant environment
levels.desc: The technology is evaluated under conditions that more consistently represent its intended application. Evidence generation becomes more structured and oriented toward reducing risk for subsequent stages.
levels.pharma: Advanced preclinical studies, CMC progress, process and product characterization, stability studies, and planning of regulatory studies, according to the asset's specific strategy.

levels.name: Demonstration in a relevant environment
levels.desc: The technology is demonstrated in an integrated way under relevant conditions, with sufficient evidence to support development decisions, technology transfer, and preparation for subsequent stages.
levels.pharma: Technically established production or synthesis process at a scale compatible with the development stage, asset characterization, generation of preclinical evidence, and technical documentation aligned with the development, transfer, and regulatory-progression strategy.

levels.name: Demonstration in an operational environment
levels.desc: The technology reaches an advanced development stage and begins to be evaluated under use or application conditions close to its intended operational environment.
levels.pharma: Start or advancement of clinical development, when applicable, accompanied by progress in CMC, production, quality control, and regulatory strategy.

levels.name: Complete and qualified system
levels.desc: The technology shows a high degree of maturity, with its main components qualified and robust evidence to support the final stages of development and approval.
levels.pharma: Advanced clinical development, consolidation of the production process, industrial qualification, and preparation or submission of the evidence package required for regulatory approval, according to the therapeutic modality and applicable jurisdiction.

levels.name: System deployed in operation
levels.desc: The technology reaches operational maturity and its application is proven in a real-world setting.
levels.pharma: Medicine or technology in use following applicable approvals, with established production and operation, and ongoing generation of real-world safety, effectiveness, and performance evidence.

TRLPage.approachHeading: Advancing maturity while preserving the asset's strategic value.
TRLPage.approachText: Every advance in maturity represents both a technical evolution and a strategic decision. Generating the necessary evidence matters just as much as building, throughout development, an asset that is scientifically robust, technically transferable, and strategically positioned for partnerships and licensing.
principios: Independent scientific governance at every stage, with specialized oversight.
Technical documentation built progressively and aligned with applicable regulatory requirements.
Intellectual property strategy conducted in parallel with scientific and technological progress.
Public and private funding matched to each project's maturity and needs.
Engagement with universities, research centers, CROs, and industrial partners at the right point in development.
Progressive preparation for technology transfer, partnerships, and licensing in the global pharmaceutical market.
TRLPage.quote: Managing technology-readiness advancement while preserving and strategically enhancing the value of intellectual property.
